question.content:
Tobin tried to define a translation.

- Point $A$ maps to point $A'$.
- Every point $P$ maps to point $P'$ such that $\overline{PP'}$ has the same length as $\overline{AA'}$.

**What mistake did Tobin make in her definition of a translation?**

[[☃ radio 1]]

choices.clue: A translation moves all points in the same direction, so $\overrightarrow{PP'}$ needs to be parallel $\overrightarrow{AA'}$. They won't intersect and form and angle.
choices.content: Tobin needed to define an angle $\theta$ formed by $\overrightarrow{AA'}$ and $\overrightarrow{PP'}$.

choices.clue: A translation moves all points in the same direction. As long as the length of $\overrightarrow{AA'}$ isn't zero, no point will map to itself in a translation.
choices.content: Tobin needed to mention which points map to themselves.

choices.clue: We need to include direction in the definition of a translation, otherwise there are infinitely many possible points for $P'$.
choices.content: $\overrightarrow{PP'}$ must be parallel to $\overrightarrow{AA'}$ and point in the same direction as $\overrightarrow{AA'}$.

choices.clue: There is more than one possible point $P'$ we could draw from Tobin's definition. What additional information does the definition need to clarify which point is the image of point $P$?
choices.content: Tobin did not make a mistake.
